status.en: 113 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 22% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 113 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 22 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits are threatening to disrupt the 2027 elections in Zamfara by blockading roads and levying fees on communities, while soldiers have cleared bandits from a forest hideout in Kogi and recovered firearms. In Plateau, troops repelled a Berom militia attack on the Ruga Madaki Auwalu community and gunmen in military uniforms killed a 60-year-old security guard and wounded two others. A funeral-bound boat capsized, killing at least 24 people. Atiku Abubakar condemned a machete attack on former footballer Segun Odegbadi, and suspected herders attacked Benue communities and a military base, rescuing two women. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Bandittene truer med å forstyrre valget i Zamfara i 2027 ved å blokkere veier og kreve avgifter fra lokalsamfunn, mens soldater har ryddet banditter fra en skogshule i Kogi og funnet tilbake skytevåpen. I Plateau avviste tropper et angrep fra Berom-milits på lokalsamfunnet Ruga Madaki Auwalu, og væpnede menn i militæruniformer drepte en 60‑år gammel sikkerhetsvakt og såret to andre. En båt på vei til begravelse kantret og drepte minst 24 personer. Atiku Abubakar fordømte et machettangrep på den tidligere fotballspilleren Segun Odegbadi, og mistenkte gjeterangrep rammet lokalsamfunn i Benue og en militærbase, der to kvinner ble reddet. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
